_comment: Per-chunk gzip ceilings, enforced by scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs as part of postbuild.
Each ceiling sits just above the value measured when it was set — a ratchet, like the
coverage thresholds in vitest.config.ts. Raising one is a deliberate reviewed change,
recorded in the commit message; a ceiling that drifts up on its own measures nothing.
gzip because nginx.conf enables gzip only, so that is what this deployment ships.
The two kinds of ceiling behave differently, on purpose. INITIAL JS and CSS cap what every
user downloads before first paint, and every route is code-split, so a new screen should
not move them: hold them, and treat a breach as a regression. The total sums every emitted
chunk, lazy ones included, so it grows with each code-split screen by construction; size it
from a real `npm run build` with headroom under the 50 kB unmatched-chunk warning in
check-bundle-size.mjs (so a new dependency cannot hide inside it), and raise it deliberately
when a feature lands. If the initial ceiling ever comes under pressure, `motion` is the
largest thing on the critical path after react-dom, and LazyMotion + domAnimation is the one
real trim, paid for by dropping layout animations such as the sidebar's active pill.
2026-09-28: every ceiling lowered after the base-project conversion removed the original
product's domain screens (package.json did not change). Measured on `npm run build`: initial
JS 193.0 kB, initial CSS 13.4 kB, total 248.3 kB gzip across 24 JS+CSS chunks. Ceilings are
now 198 / 16 / 260 kB: the same headroom the initial ceilings had before (about 5 and 2.5
kB), and 11.7 kB on the total, room for a typical code-split screen and well under the 50 kB
unmatched-chunk warning. The old 380 kB total was sized for screens that no longer exist.
2026-09-29: total raised 260 -> 272 kB for the Projects screens (workspace sidebar, board,
list view, issue drawer), which land as their own lazy chunk. Measured on `npm run build`:
total 261.7 kB gzip, of which the new feature is 10.9 kB (9.6 kB lazy chunk, 0.5 kB initial
JS for the nav icon and routes, 0.3 kB CSS, ~0.5 kB from shared code splitting further).
The initial ceilings did not move: initial JS 193.9 / 198 kB, initial CSS 13.7 / 16 kB.
272 restores the ~10 kB of total headroom the previous setting left for the next screen.
2026-10-05: total raised 272 -> 288 kB for time tracking (the issue drawer's time panel and
timer, the Timesheet screen, the header's running-timer indicator). Measured on `npm run
build`: total 276.9 kB gzip, up 14.8 kB, of which the Timesheet is its own 4.8 kB lazy chunk,
the drawer's panel grows the projects chunk 10.1 -> 14.7 kB, and the header's menu is a 1.2 kB
chunk loaded only while a timer runs. Initial JS 195.1 / 198 kB (+1.2 kB: the timer slice,
its four API calls and the date-key helper, which the header needs on every screen). It was
196.9 before the parser, week maths and the menu were split out of the initial chunk, which is
the reason those modules are separate files. 288 leaves ~11 kB of total headroom, as before.

total 304.8 kB gzip, up 27.9 kB, of which the reports screens are their own 21.3 kB lazy chunk
(hand-drawn SVG, no chart library), the sprint panel grows the
projects chunk 14.7 -> 17.0 kB, and shared UI that both now use (switch, StatusBadge,
useKeyed) splits into small common chunks. Initial JS 196.0 / 198 kB (+0.9 kB: the nav entry,
the four lazy routes and the client's file-download mode). Initial CSS 14.0 / 16 kB (+0.3 kB
print styles). 316 leaves ~11 kB of total headroom, as before.
